answer: The catalogue should not assert a direct 'learned repertoire from' property between the two Persons (E21). CRM has no such property, and P152 has parent -- the one property the SIG did sanction directly between two E21 instances despite an event path existing (P98i/E67/P96/P97) -- shows that direct actor-to-actor shortcuts are only added when the SIG deliberately decides a relation is universally query-relevant (Minimality; Extensions of CIDOC CRM: 'only concepts to be used for selecting multiple instances ... by formal querying need to be explicitly modelled'). No comparable decision exists for teaching/apprenticeship. Instead, each of the 40 tapes documents a session, modelled as an E7 Activity (both fiddlers as P11 had participant / P14 carried out by), each tape as a document (E31/E22) that P70 documents the activity. 'Grandnephew learned his repertoire from his granduncle' is the community-level pattern that this population of individual activities is evidence for -- exactly Martin Doerr's answer in the 'Recording Intangible Cultural Heritage' thread (t0916), which splits intangible heritage into (A) particular performances, (B) a type of activity characteristic of a community/tradition, evidenced by individual events, and (C) oral tradition as an Information Object carried by people. This case is sense (B): 'Each pattern is supported by evidence by individual events.' So: represent the sessions as events; let the teacher/student relation be an inference over them, not a base-CRM property.

rejected_alternatives.option: A direct E21->E21 shortcut property (analogous to P152 has parent) for 'learned from'/'taught by'
rejected_alternatives.why_not: connect E21 E21 shows the only property the CRM declares directly on the Person-Person pair is P152 has parent, created by explicit SIG decision as a shortcut for the birth-event path; no equivalent shortcut for teaching/apprenticeship exists in the ontology, and Minimality/Extensions of CIDOC CRM narrative says such shortcuts are added only when needed for general querying, not per-case.

rejected_alternatives.option: Treating the relationship as fully out of scope for CRM
rejected_alternatives.why_not: t0916 (Martin Doerr, Christian-Emil Ore, Nicola Carboni) establishes CRM can and does represent this kind of intangible transmission -- as events with participants plus a supported higher-level pattern -- so it is in scope, just not via a direct property.

citations.quote: Each pattern is supported by evidence by individual events.

citations: Modelling principles > Extensions of CIDOC CRM
